title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases

articles.content_en:
For the purposes of these Provisions, private lending refers to the act of financing between natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations.
Disputes arising from related financial business such as granting loans by financial institutions and their branches that are established upon approval by the financial regulatory authority to engage in loan business shall not be governed by these Provisions.

When a lender brings a private lending action in a People's Court, it shall provide debt instruments such as IOUs, receipts, and promissory notes, as well as other evidence capable of proving the existence of the lending legal relationship.
Where the debt instruments such as IOUs, receipts, and promissory notes held by a party do not specify the creditor, and the party holding the debt instruments brings a private lending action, the People's Court shall accept the case. If the defendant raises a defense against the plaintiff's creditor qualification with factual basis, and the People's Court finds upon examination that the plaintiff does not have creditor qualification, it shall rule to dismiss the action.

Where the lending and borrowing parties have not agreed on the place of performance of the contract, or the agreement is unclear, and no supplementary agreement is reached afterwards, and it still cannot be determined according to the relevant terms of the contract or trade practices, the place where the party receiving the money is located shall be the place of performance of the contract.

Where a surety provides joint and several liability suretyship for the borrower, and the lender only sues the borrower, the People's Court may not add the surety as a co-defendant; where the lender only sues the surety, the People's Court may add the borrower as a co-defendant.
Where a surety provides general suretyship for the borrower, and the lender only sues the surety, the People's Court shall add the borrower as a co-defendant; where the lender only sues the borrower, the People's Court may not add the surety as a co-defendant.

After a People's Court files a case, if it discovers that the private lending act itself is suspected of crimes such as illegal fundraising, it shall rule to dismiss the action and transfer the clues and materials of suspected crimes such as illegal fundraising to the public security organ or the procuratorial organ.
Where the public security organ or the procuratorial organ decides not to file the case, or revokes the case after filing and investigation, or the procuratorial organ makes a decision not to prosecute, or a legally effective judgment of the People's Court determines that it does not constitute a crime such as illegal fundraising, and the party brings an action in the People's Court on the same facts again, the People's Court shall accept the case.

After a People's Court files a case, if it discovers clues or materials of suspected crimes such as illegal fundraising that are related to the private lending dispute case but are not the same facts, the People's Court shall continue to hear the private lending dispute case and transfer the clues and materials of suspected crimes such as illegal fundraising to the public security organ or the procuratorial organ.

Where the basic facts of a private lending dispute case must be based on the trial result of a criminal case, and the criminal case has not yet been concluded, the People's Court shall rule to suspend the action.

Where the borrower is suspected of committing a crime, or a legally effective judgment determines that he is guilty, and the lender sues requesting the surety to bear civil liability, the People's Court shall accept the case.

For private lending contracts concluded between legal persons, between unincorporated organizations, or between them for the needs of production and operation, except where the circumstances provided for in Article 146, Article 153, or Article 154 of the Civil Code and Article 13 of these Provisions exist, if a party asserts that the private lending contract is valid, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Where a legal person or an unincorporated organization raises funds from its employees within the entity in the form of borrowing, for the production and operation of the entity, and none of the circumstances provided for in Article 144, Article 146, Article 153, or Article 154 of the Civil Code and Article 13 of these Provisions exists, if a party asserts that the private lending contract is valid, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Where the borrowing or lending act of the borrower or lender is suspected of committing a crime, or a legally effective judgment has determined that it constitutes a crime, and a party initiates a civil action, the private lending contract is not automatically void. The People's Court shall determine the validity of the private lending contract in accordance with Article 144, Article 146, Article 153, and Article 154 of the Civil Code and Article 13 of these Provisions.
Where a surety asserts that it shall not bear civil liability on the ground that the borrowing or lending act of the borrower or lender is suspected of committing a crime or has been determined by a legally effective judgment to constitute a crime, the People's Court shall, in accordance with the validity of the private lending contract and the suretyship contract and the degree of fault of the parties, determine the civil liability of the surety according to law.

Where the plaintiff brings a private lending action on the basis of debt instruments such as IOUs, receipts, and promissory notes, and the defendant raises a defense or counterclaim on the basis of the underlying legal relationship and provides evidence proving that the debt dispute is not caused by a private lending act, the People's Court shall, according to the ascertained facts of the case, hear the case in accordance with the underlying legal relationship.
The preceding paragraph shall not apply to debt and credit agreements reached by the parties through mediation, conciliation, or liquidation.

Where the plaintiff brings a private lending action solely on the basis of debt instruments such as IOUs, receipts, and promissory notes, and the defendant defends that the loan has already been repaid, the defendant shall provide evidence to prove its claim. After the defendant provides corresponding evidence to prove its claim, the plaintiff shall still bear the burden of adducing evidence for the existence of the lending relationship.
Where the defendant defends that the lending act has not actually occurred and can provide a reasonable explanation, the People's Court shall, in light of the loan amount, delivery of funds, the economic capacity of the parties, the local or inter-party transaction methods, trade practices, changes in the parties' property, and witness testimony and other facts and factors, comprehensively determine whether the lending fact has occurred.

Where the plaintiff brings a private lending action solely on the basis of a transfer voucher of a financial institution, and the defendant defends that the transfer was for repayment of a previous loan or other debt between the parties, the defendant shall provide evidence to prove its claim. After the defendant provides corresponding evidence to prove its claim, the plaintiff shall still bear the burden of adducing evidence for the formation of the lending relationship.

Pursuant to paragraph 2 of Article 174 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, where the plaintiff bearing the burden of adducing evidence refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, and upon examination the existing evidence cannot confirm the main facts of the case such as the lending act, loan amount, and method of payment, the People's Court shall not recognize the facts asserted by the plaintiff.

Where it is found upon investigation that the action is a false private lending action, and the plaintiff applies to withdraw the action, the People's Court shall not permit it and shall, pursuant to Article 112 of the Civil Procedure Law, enter a judgment to dismiss its claims.
Where a participant in the proceedings or any other person maliciously creates or participates in a false action, the People's Court shall, pursuant to Articles 111, 112, and 113 of the Civil Procedure Law, impose a fine or detention according to law; where the act constitutes a crime, the case shall be transferred to the judicial organ with jurisdiction for investigation of criminal liability.
Where an entity maliciously creates or participates in a false action, the People's Court shall impose a fine on the entity, and may also impose a fine or detention on its principal responsible person or directly responsible personnel; where the act constitutes a crime, the case shall be transferred to the judicial organ with jurisdiction for investigation of criminal liability.

Where a person signs or affixes a seal on debt instruments such as IOUs, receipts, and promissory notes or on a loan contract, but does not indicate his identity as a surety or assumption of suretyship liability, or cannot be presumed to be a surety through other facts, if the lender requests him to bear suretyship liability, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Where a lending relationship is formed between the lending and borrowing parties through an online lending platform, and the provider of the online lending platform only provides intermediary services, if a party requests it to bear guarantee liability, the People's Court shall not support the request.
Where the provider of the online lending platform clearly states through web pages, advertisements, or other media, or there is other evidence proving that it provides a guarantee for the loan, and the lender requests the provider of the online lending platform to bear guarantee liability, the People's Court shall support the request.

Where the legal representative of a legal person or the person in charge of an unincorporated organization signs a private lending contract with the lender in the name of the entity, and there is evidence proving that the borrowed funds are used personally by the legal representative or person in charge, if the lender requests that the legal representative or person in charge be listed as a co-defendant or a third party, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where the legal representative of a legal person or the person in charge of an unincorporated organization concludes a private lending contract with the lender in his personal name, and the borrowed funds are used for the production and operation of the entity, if the lender requests the entity and the individual to bear liability jointly, the People's Court shall support the request.

Where the parties use the conclusion of a sale and purchase contract as a guarantee for a private lending contract, and after the loan becomes due, the borrower is unable to repay the loan, and the lender requests performance of the sale and purchase contract, the People's Court shall hear the case in accordance with the private lending legal relationship. Where a party changes its claims based on the circumstances of the court hearing, the People's Court shall permit it.
After the judgment rendered by hearing in accordance with the private lending legal relationship takes effect, if the borrower fails to perform the monetary debt determined in the effective judgment, the lender may apply for auction of the subject matter of the sale and purchase contract to repay the debt. With respect to the difference between the proceeds from the auction and the loan principal and interest to be repaid, the borrower or the lender has the right to claim return or compensation.

Where the lending and borrowing parties have not agreed on interest, and the lender claims payment of interest, the People's Court shall not support the claim.
Where natural persons have unclear agreement on interest in a loan, and the lender claims payment of interest, the People's Court shall not support the claim. Except for loans between natural persons, where the lending and borrowing parties have unclear agreement on loan interest, and the lender claims interest, the People's Court shall determine the interest in light of the content of the private lending contract and based on factors such as the local or inter-party transaction methods, trade practices, and market quote rate.

Where the lender requests the borrower to pay interest at the interest rate agreed in the contract, the People's Court shall support the request, except where the interest rate agreed by the parties exceeds four times the one-year loan market quote rate at the time of the formation of the contract.
The "one-year loan market quote rate" referred to in the preceding paragraph means the one-year loan market quote rate published monthly by the National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China since August 20, 2019.

The loan amount stated in debt instruments such as IOUs, receipts, and promissory notes is generally determined to be the principal. Where interest is deducted from the principal in advance, the People's Court shall determine the actual amount lent as the principal.

Where the lending and borrowing parties, after settling the principal and interest of the previous loan, include the interest in the principal of the subsequent loan and reissue a debt instrument, if the interest rate of the previous period does not exceed four times the one-year loan market quote rate at the time of the formation of the contract, the amount stated in the reissued debt instrument may be determined as the principal of the subsequent loan. Interest exceeding that portion shall not be determined as the principal of the subsequent loan.
If, calculated according to the preceding paragraph, the total principal and interest that the borrower shall pay after the expiration of the loan period exceeds the sum of the initial loan principal and the interest for the entire loan period calculated at four times the one-year loan market quote rate at the time of the formation of the contract with the initial loan principal as the base, the People's Court shall not support the excess.

Where the lending and borrowing parties have agreed on an overdue interest rate, such agreement shall prevail, provided that it does not exceed four times the one-year loan market quote rate at the time of the formation of the contract.
Where no overdue interest rate is agreed, or the agreement is unclear, the People's Court may handle it by distinguishing different situations:
(1) If neither the in-term interest rate nor the overdue interest rate is agreed, and the lender claims that the borrower shall bear liability for breach of contract for overdue repayment with interest calculated by reference to the one-year loan market quote rate at that time from the date of overdue repayment, the People's Court shall support the claim;
(2) If the in-term interest rate is agreed but the overdue interest rate is not agreed, and the lender claims that the borrower shall pay interest for the period of fund occupation at the in-term interest rate from the date of overdue repayment, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Where the lender and the borrower have agreed on both an overdue interest rate and liquidated damages or other fees, the lender may choose to claim overdue interest, liquidated damages, or other fees, or may claim them together, but the portion exceeding four times the one-year loan market quote rate at the time of the formation of the contract in total shall not be supported by the People's Court.

The borrower may repay the loan in advance, except where the parties otherwise agree.
Where the borrower repays the loan in advance and claims that interest shall be calculated based on the actual loan period, the People's Court shall support the claim.

After these Provisions come into force, new first-instance private lending dispute cases accepted by the People's Court shall be governed by these Provisions.
For first-instance private lending cases newly accepted after August 20, 2020, where the loan contract was concluded before August 20, 2020, and a party requests that the judicial interpretation then in effect be applied to calculate the interest portion from the conclusion of the contract to August 19, 2020, the People's Court shall support the request; for the interest portion from August 20, 2020 to the date of repayment of the loan, the interest protection standard of these Provisions at the time of filing of the action shall apply.
After these Provisions come into force, where the relevant judicial interpretations previously made by the Supreme People's Court are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
